title: Canonical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions
source_anchor: Optlib pinned commit 5da27c5f95aa6a8a45b8c14b968ade4c13ff18c3, Optlib/Convex/StronglyConvex.lean, theorem Strong_Convex_second_lower; Chewi Lectures on Optimization v1, Proposition 1.6 equation (1.4)
target_statement: Port the pinned Optlib theorem stating that strong convexity plus a supplied gradient on a convex domain implies f(y) >= f(x) + <grad f(x), y-x> + m/2 ||y-x||^2, as one ASTIS-owned shared declaration reusable by Optimization Chapter 1, Sampling Chapter 2, and OT convex-potential arguments.

searched: Samplinglib: Geometry/StrongConvexity.lean, Analysis/ConvexSubgradient.lean, Geometry/GeodesicConvexity.lean, Analysis/Calculus/Gradient.lean, Registry.lean
Mathlib: Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Strong; no existing higher-dimensional first-order lower-bound declaration found in the audited API
Optlib pinned 5da27c5f95aa6a8a45b8c14b968ade4c13ff18c3: exact theorem Strong_Convex_second_lower found
CvxLean: no exact StrongConvexOn/gradient first-order theorem found in repository search
shared_floor_audit.notes: Do not reprove a route-local copy. Port the exact upstream mathematical statement into an ASTIS-owned module using current Mathlib/ASTIS primitives; keep Gibbs/log-concavity adapters downstream.

consulted.hypothesis_adapter: ASTIS uses Mathlib StrongConvexOn normalization m/2 * ||x-y||^2, matching Optlib and Chewi's alpha/2 normalization.

Chewi states the whole-space C1 specialization; the canonical shared theorem follows the already-formal Optlib domain-local gradient formulation. Source-facing Chewi wrappers must specialize it without claiming the generalization is Chewi's exact statement.

source_detail_audit.fidelity_boundary: The ASTIS declaration ports the pinned Optlib theorem shape. Chewi Proposition 1.6 is a downstream specialization, not silently relabeled as the more general shared statement.
